title: Throughput SLO bands, burn-rate policy, and crediting matrix for Dedicated capacity contracts
creator: Daniel Kim
body:
Summary:
This ticket defines a concrete, auditable approach for Dedicated throughput Service Level Objectives (SLOs), associated error budget definitions, burn-rate policies tied to autoscaling and fleet controls, and an operational crediting/compensation matrix suitable for inclusion in customer contracts. The goal is to provide legal-facing contract language plus the engineering metrics and runbook needed to measure and respond to breaches while minimizing customer downtime and economic exposure.

Goals and constraints:
- Provide deterministic throughput guarantees in terms customers can contract against (tokens/sec per reserved GPU pool, or requests/sec depending on route).
- Define error budgets and burn-rate rules that map to operational responses (autoscale, graceful degradation, fallbacks).
- Produce a crediting matrix that is simple to calculate for billing and legal teams and defensible by SRE/observability data.
- Ensure the SLOs integrate with autoscaling policies and fleet controls without creating perverse incentives (e.g., artificially inflating credits by delaying autoscale).

Key definitions (engineer-friendly):
- Reservation: a committed capacity bundle (GPU count + instance type + memory) reserved by customer for Dedicated.
- Provisioned Throughput (PT): the expected sustained throughput capacity for a reservation, expressed as tokens/sec or requests/sec at a canonical prompt mix. Each reservation has a PT value assigned at onboarding by Model Onboarding team.
- Observed Throughput (OT): aggregated real-time measured throughput served to the customer over a measurement window.
- Availability for throughput (AT): AT = min(1, OT / PT) computed over the rolling measurement window.
- SLO target: the contractual target for AT (e.g., 99.5% availability of provisioned throughput over a 30-day window).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO_target expressed as a percentage of total PT-time per measurement window.

Metric primitives and measurement windows:
- Primary measurement window: 30d rolling window for contractually binding availability and credit calculation.
- Short-term windows: 1h and 24h windows used for operational automation and burn-rate calculation.
- Sampling cadence: 1m aggregated buckets (aligned to UTC minute).
- Canonical prompt mix: set of representative request size/seq distributions defined at onboarding and used to normalize PT. If customer workload diverges significantly from canonical mix, parties will recontract PT or switch to request-level SLO.

SLO bands and examples (proposal):
- Platinum: 99.95% throughput availability over 30d (error budget = 0.05% of PT-time).
- Gold: 99.9% over 30d (error budget 0.1%).
- Silver: 99.5% over 30d (error budget 0.5%).
- Bronze: 99.0% over 30d (error budget 1.0%).
Notes: band selection determines price and allowed autoscaling behavior (see "Autoscale integration" below).

Error budget accounting and burn-rate policy:
- Error budget is consumed when AT < 1 for a minute bucket. Budget consumption per minute = (1 - AT) * PT * 60s (normalized to PT-time).
- Burn-rate is computed as the ratio of error budget consumed in a short-term window to the error budget remaining for the 30d window.
- Automated responses based on burn-rate (recommended):
  - Burn-rate < 1: normal operation; generate alert if sustained trend upward.
  - Burn-rate between 1 and 4: elevated; trigger investigation, optional application throttling or cache tuning, and notify account team.
  - Burn-rate > 4: critical; escalate to on-call SRE, consider immediate autoscale (if policy allows), enable degraded fallback model variant, and apply rate-limiting on non-critical routes.
- Burn-rate thresholds are tunable per customer tier and may be included as appendices in contracts.

Interplay with autoscaling and fleet controls:
- Autoscaling modes (per-reservation):
  - Locked: no autoscale; customer capacity fixed. Breaches in Locked reservations produce credits per matrix below without capacity-level autoscale attempts.
  - Adaptive: autoscale allowed up to X% burst capacity or to a max pool size defined in contract. Autoscale decisions must be recorded (timestamp, new capacity, reason) and considered when assigning credits to avoid double-counting.
  - Fallback-enabled: if autoscale fails or is constrained, system may route to compatible hosted model variants or degraded quantized variants subject to customer policy.
- To avoid the moral hazard where autoscale is used to avoid credits, contract language will specify a small time window (e.g., 15 minutes) preceding a capacity change that is attributable to the breach and is used in credit calculation.
- Fleet controls (regional affinity, instance-type constraints) declared at provisioning influence the autoscale headroom and therefore the SLO/PT calculation. Customers that restrict fleet controls accept correspondingly lower PT or lower SLO band unless compensated by price.

Crediting and financial remediation matrix (illustrative):
- Credit basis: monetary credits expressed as percentage of monthly Dedicated fee proportional to PT-time lost. Credits are capped (e.g., max 50% of monthly Dedicated fee for repeated outages) and subject to maximum aggregate per rolling 12 months.
- Example simple formula: Credit = Monthly_fee * (Budget_time_lost / Total_month_time) * Band_multiplier, where Band_multiplier is 1.0 for Silver, 1.5 for Gold, 2.0 for Platinum (reflects stricter guarantees).
- Discrete credit tiers for quick contract language:
  - Loss <= error budget: no credit.
  - Loss > error budget and <= 2x error budget: 10% monthly fee credit for affected reservation segment.
  - Loss > 2x and <= 5x: 25% credit.
  - Loss > 5x: 50% credit + right to request expedited remediation or termination for material breach (subject to cure period).
Notes: the above is intentionally conservative; legal should review for enforceability and regional regulatory constraints.

Operational detection and runbook (SRE):
- Detection: automated alert triggers when 1m bucket AT < 0.98 for two contiguous buckets or when burn-rate exceeds 1 in 1h window.
- Triage steps (1-15 minutes):
  1) Triage on-call reviews recent capacity changes and autoscale history.
  2) Confirm measurement integrity (telemetry backfill, Prometheus scrape health, ingestion pipeline latency).
  3) Validate whether canonical prompt mix deviation explains shortfall (compare request histograms).
- Mitigation steps (15-60 minutes):
  1) If adaptive autoscale allowed, trigger manual scale-up to contracted max and document.
  2) If autoscale not available or unsuccessful, enable fallback model variant or apply graceful request queuing with SLAs for interactive routes.
  3) If root cause is kernel inefficiency or model regression, engage Model Ops; schedule immediate hotfix if possible.
- Post-incident: calculate PT-time lost, update error budget ledger, and compute credits per contract rules.

Contract language - sample snippets (for legal):
- Definition of Throughput SLO: "Service Throughput SLO" means the percentage of Provisioned Throughput (PT) made available to Customer during the 30-day measurement window, as measured by Redwood Inference per the Measurement Methodology in Appendix A.
- Credit remedy: "If Redwood fails to meet the Service Throughput SLO set forth for the Customer's reservation, Customer shall be eligible to receive Service Credits calculated in accordance with the Crediting Matrix in Appendix B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a claim to Redwood within 30 days of the end of the measurement window. Credits shall be Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for a breach of the Service Throughput SLO, except as set forth in Section X (Material Breach)."
- Autoscale and attribution clause: "Where the Customer has configured the Reservation to permit Redwood-managed autoscaling, Redwood shall document any capacity changes and attribute their timing to the measurement stream. Capacity changes that occur within fifteen (15) minutes prior to or during an availability shortfall will be considered in credit calculation to avoid double remediation for the same event."
- Termination right for repeated breaches: "If in any rolling 90-day period Redwood fails to meet the Service Throughput SLO for three (3) or more measurement windows, Customer may provide written notice to Redwood to cure the deficiency. If Redwood fails to cure within thirty (30) days, Customer may terminate the Agreement for material breach and receive a pro rata refund of unused pre-paid Dedicated fees."

Monitoring, evidence and dispute resolution:
- Evidence for any credit claim will be the standard telemetry ledger (1m buckets) stored in the customer's audit view for 365 days. Both parties will use UTC timestamps and agreed canonical prompt mix.
- Disputes will follow a two-step process: (1) technical review with SRE + customer engineers (7 days), (2) escalation to legal + account teams for arbitration if unresolved (30 days).

Open decisions and tradeoffs:
- Whether to expose per-route SLOs vs. only per-reservation PT SLOs. Per-route adds precision but increases measurement complexity.
- Final numeric multipliers for credit matrix (band_multiplier) — needs legal and finance sign-off.
- Allowed autoscale headroom and attribution window length (we propose 15 minutes but could be 5-30).
